source: IAPWS Wagner-Pruss auxiliary saturation; vapour heat capacity: the Shomate form (A..E) fitted to the IAPWS-95 ideal-gas Cp (CoolProp Water.json EOS[0].alpha0, CoolProp 8.0.0 (github.com/CoolProp/CoolProp ae81610e, MIT)) over 273.16..900 K, worst 0.054 %, with F and H from the ATcT 1.220 formation enthalpy -241.808 kJ/mol (CoolProp master 9b35f538 INFO.STANDARD_STATE) so that h(298.15 K) = 0 (tools/open-thermo-data/derive.mjs, batch 2026-11-04-open-thermo-data); Watson latent heat; ice Ih below the melting line (crystal record and IAPWS R14-08 sublimation pressure, WP4 of batch 2026-09-24-coolprop-low-temperature)

thermochemistry.source: Ideal-gas heat of formation at 298.15 K and formula H2O (molar mass 18.015 g/mol) of ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Water" (ChemSep index 1921, CAS 7732-18-5). ChemSep's value, the basis of every other heat here; the water model's Shomate constants use ATcT 1.220's -241808 J/mol. Heats of reaction follow by Hess's law. Data only.

liquid.source: IAPWS SR6-08(2011), equation 7 and table 5; coefficients converted from microPa.s to Pa.s. https://iapws.org/technical-guidance/release/LiquidWater.download . Includes metastable liquid below freezing and above boiling at 0.1 MPa; this is not a phase-stability model.

sublimation_pressure.source: IAPWS R14-08(2011), Revised Release on the Pressure along the Melting and Sublimation Curves of Ordinary Water Substance, equation 6 with table 3: ln(p_sub/p_t) = (T_t/T) sum a_i (T/T_t)^b_i at the triple point of the ice record (273.16 K, 611.657 Pa); free release https://iapws.org; its check value 8.94735 Pa at 230 K reproduced (tools/unified-thermo-port-ice/fit). The free-water rule scales it to meet the liquid's saturation pressure on the melting line (FreeWaterIce).
